chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from the one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from his father, who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when the fruits reached maturity, ordered that the walls be grooved.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (SAWW) do when fruits reached maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) institutionalized generosity, where he mandated the grooving of orchard walls (*thulimat*) to facilitate public access to ripe produce. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on social welfare and the removal of barriers to sustenance, reflecting the principle that natural resources should be accessible to the community during peak harvest.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from the one who narrated it to him, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim Al Ja’fary, from his father who said,
‘It was so that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, when the fruits reached (maturity), ordered with the walls, so they were grooved (for people to come inside and eat their fill)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasaniy from those who narrated to him from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja‘fariy from his father who has said the following: “
When fruits ripened the Holy prophet would command to open gaps in the walls (of the gardens for people passing by).”’
